classification.difficultyReason: Translate the specified 60-degree clockwise rotation into two grid divisions, preserve each endpoint's circle, and join the image endpoints.

content.prompt: Rotate the interval $AB$ by $60^{\circ}$ in a clockwise direction about the point $O$.

spec.description: Square polar scaffold with five concentric circles and rays every 30 degrees. The labelled interval requires free-form TikZ because a blank-grid template cannot express polar circles, rays and supplied endpoints.
spec.mathematics: O is the centre. A is on circle 2 at polar angle 240 degrees; B is on circle 4 at polar angle 300 degrees. Polar angles are measured anticlockwise from the rightward horizontal.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the original interval AB and centre O are supplied; no image endpoints are visible.

answer.short: $A'$ lies on the second circle directly left of $O$; $B'$ lies on the fourth circle, $30^{\circ}$ left of the downward vertical. Join $A'$ to $B'$.
answer.worked: $60^{\circ}=2\times30^{\circ}$. Move each endpoint two radial divisions clockwise, keeping it on its original circle. Thus $A'$ is directly left of $O$ on the second circle, and $B'$ is on the fourth circle, $30^{\circ}$ left of the downward vertical. Join and label the image interval $A'B'$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2; answer evidence PDF page 57, printed page 604
spec.description: Complete polar scaffold showing the original blue interval and its red rotated image.
spec.mathematics: Clockwise rotation subtracts 60 degrees: A at radius 2 and angle 240 degrees maps to radius 2 and angle 180 degrees; B at radius 4 and angle 300 degrees maps to radius 4 and angle 240 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Answer-only complete construction with A', B' and the joined image interval.
